response.sql: SELECT AVG(item_ratio) AS overall_avg_ratio, AVG(line_count) AS avg_line_items_per_order_item FROM (SELECT order_item_id, AVG(product_price * 1.0 / NULLIF(derived_total_cost, 0)) AS item_ratio, COUNT(*) AS line_count FROM Invoice_Line_Items GROUP BY order_item_id) t

assumptions.assumption: Order items are those that appear in Invoice_Line_Items, so order items with no invoice line items are left out of both averages.
A derived_total_cost of 0 gives a missing ratio, which is skipped. NULL prices or costs are skipped the same way.
The overall ratio is the plain average of the per-item average ratios, with each order item weighted equally. Order items whose ratios are all missing are ignored.

alternatives.interpretation: Include every order item from Order_Items. Those with no invoice line items count as 0 line items. Their ratio is missing, so they are ignored in the ratio average.
alternatives.sql: SELECT AVG(item_ratio) AS overall_avg_ratio, AVG(line_count) AS avg_line_items_per_order_item FROM (SELECT oi.order_item_id, AVG(ili.product_price * 1.0 / NULLIF(ili.derived_total_cost, 0)) AS item_ratio, COUNT(ili.order_item_id) AS line_count FROM Order_Items oi LEFT JOIN Invoice_Line_Items ili ON ili.order_item_id = oi.order_item_id GROUP BY oi.order_item_id) t
